verdict.rationale: PagerDuty documents a first-party mobile app for responding to incidents on the go, with mobile schedules and widgets. Community users confirm they acknowledge pages from the app, sometimes after being woken by a phone call. Escalating and resolving from the phone are not explicitly documented; they are only implied by the generic 'respond to incidents'. One older report says acknowledgement failed mid-crisis, but it does not tie that failure to the app. missing for 10: explicit documentation of escalate and resolve actions in the mobile app, independent corroboration of mobile resolve/escalate workflows.

support.subject: As an on-call engineer, a full mobile app lets me acknowledge, escalate, and resolve from my phone at 3am

citations.quote: The PagerDuty mobile app allows you to respond to incidents, view account objects, and manage settings on the go, wherever you are.
Engineers never need to actually use the PagerDuty website and only use the app for ack'ing the page.
If you have the app it will first try to notify through the app. If there is no ack within a couple of minutes it calls you.
